title: Python SDK service-specific behavior for ZIA: admin, AppTotal, browser control, smart isolation and GRE tunnel VIPs

prose.text: These are claims about the Python SDK's service helpers, not about ZIA. Each covers one behavior a reader would otherwise have to infer from the method signature.

convert-to-user-spec.statement: The API specification describes `POST /adminUsers/{userId}/convertToUser` as removing a user's admin privileges while keeping them as a regular user, as an alternative to DELETE, which removes the admin and also removes them as a user. It says the admin user's details are first obtained with `GET /users` and then sent in the convert request.

expect.description:
Removes admin privileges for a user while retaining them as a regular user of your organization in the ZIA Admin Portal. This can be used as an alternative to the DELETE /adminUsers/{userId} request, which deletes an admin and removes them as a user from the ZIA Admin Portal. To learn more, see Deleting ZIA Admins.

Before you can delete the admin privileges for a user, you need to obtain the admin user's ID and other information by using the GET /users request and then send the admin user details in the POST /adminUsers/{userId}/convertToUser request.

gre-vip-auto-select-tests-camel-keys.statement: `add_gre_tunnel` and `update_gre_tunnel` document the VIPs as `primary_dest_vip` and `secondary_dest_vip` (the add docstring's example passes `primary_dest_vip` as a dict), use their keyword arguments as the body, and decide whether to pick VIPs by testing for the camelCase keys `primaryDestVip` and `secondaryDestVip`. When either camelCase key is absent they call `get_closest_diverse_vip_ids` with the source IP, which lists the recommended VIPs and raises ValueError when none is returned or none is in a second city, and they write the IDs it returns under `primaryDestVip` and `secondaryDestVip`.

quotes: Note: If the `primary_dest_vip` and `secondary_dest_vip` aren't specified then the closest recommended VIPs will be automatically chosen.
if "primaryDestVip" not in body or "secondaryDestVip" not in body:
if "primaryDestVip" not in body or "secondaryDestVip" not in body:
raise ValueError("No VIPs found for the given source IP.")
raise ValueError("No diverse VIPs found in different cities.")

upstream.note: Python SDK: add_gre_tunnel/update_gre_tunnel test camelCase primaryDestVip/secondaryDestVip while documenting snake_case primary_dest_vip/secondary_dest_vip.

gre-documented-vips-replaced.statement: So a call that passes both VIPs under the documented snake_case names still runs the VIP lookup, and fails with its ValueError when the lookup finds no diverse pair; otherwise the body holds both the caller's `primary_dest_vip` and the added `primaryDestVip`, both become the wire key `primaryDestVip` when the executor camel-cases the body, and the added key, written later, replaces the caller's value. The secondary VIP is replaced the same way, so the tunnel is sent with the recommended VIPs, not the ones passed.
gre-documented-vips-replaced.conditions: Rests on Python dict insertion order: the caller's keyword arguments are in the body before the function adds the camelCase keys, and `convert_keys_to_camel_case` assigns `result[to_lower_camel_case(k)]` in iteration order, so the later key's value is the one kept. FIELD_EXCEPTIONS has no entry for these keys: `git -C vendor/zscaler-sdk-python show <ref>:zscaler/helpers.py | sed -n '/^def to_lower_camel_case/,/^def convert_keys_to_snake_case/p' | grep -c -E '"(primary_dest_vip|secondary_dest_vip)"'` returns 0 at v1.11.3 and HEAD. Read from the code, not run against a tenant.

upstream.note: Python SDK: explicit snake_case VIPs passed to add_gre_tunnel/update_gre_tunnel are overwritten by the auto-selected VIPs.

ansible-gre-reaches-vip-replacement.statement: The ZIA Ansible collection at v2.2.4 passes a configured tunnel's VIPs to `add_gre_tunnel` and `update_gre_tunnel` as `primary_dest_vip` and `secondary_dest_vip`, so VIPs set in a playbook are subject to that replacement.

quotes: if "primaryDestVip" not in body or "secondaryDestVip" not in body:

ansible-gre-reaches-vip-replacement.conditions: Read from plugins/modules/zia_traffic_forwarding_gre_tunnels.py at v2.2.4 (HEAD); the module was not run. The SDK range: the collection's requirements.txt at v2.2.4 requires `zscaler-sdk-python>=1.9.30` with no upper bound (pyproject.toml carries the same requirement), and the camelCase auto-select guard quoted in gre-vip-auto-select-tests-camel-keys is present in add_gre_tunnel at v1.9.30 (evidence below), v1.11.3 and HEAD, so every allowed SDK release from 1.9.30 on is affected.

smart-isolation-kwarg-names.summary: Keyword names for Smart Browser Isolation user and group scoping in the Python SDK

positions.says: The docstring and example for update_smart_isolation name the keywords smart_isolation_users_ids and smart_isolation_groups_ids.

quotes: smart_isolation_users_ids (list[str]): IDs of users for which the rule is applied.

positions.says: The shared ID-remapping list names smart_isolation_user_ids and smart_isolation_group_ids, so the documented spellings are not in it.

smart-isolation-kwarg-names.impact: A caller who follows the docstring may leave the user and group ID lists unwrapped, not in the {id: ...} shape the API takes; what the API does with the unwrapped keys is not shown. Read the rule back after the call instead of trusting the call result.
